changedBeliefs: The Dart row decoder was paying to answer a question C already had the inputs for. `fastDecodeText` had to classify every TEXT cell as ASCII (Latin-1 widen) or not (utf8.decode) before it could build the String, costing a second ExternalTypedData word view plus a bounds-checked scan per cell — and falling back to a byte-by-byte loop for values under 16 bytes or on an unaligned pointer, which covers most real database text. `resqlite_step_row` holds the same pointer and length one frame earlier, in cache, where the answer is a branch-free SWAR pass.

Moving the classification into the native step loop (RESQLITE_TEXT_ASCII = type code 6) is worth a reproduced 10-24% on text-bearing select() reads, including 19-24% on the repo's canonical 6-column mixed product row, across two order-flipped AOT passes. The saving is per TEXT cell, so it scales with text carried per read rather than with row count; the 400 B lane gains most (-22.2% / -19.4%) because the replaced Dart scan walked ~50 words per cell, and the canonical mixed row gains as much as it does because its description column is ~85 bytes on its own.

Scanning a non-ASCII value all the way to the end in C, instead of bailing at the first high byte, costs nothing measurable: ordinary CJK text moved -2.4% / -1.7% and the worst case built to expose the trade (400 B with its one multibyte character at byte 0) moved +1.1% / -1.0%. The full-scan shape buys a single branch on the common all-ASCII path, and any value that fails the test is about to be walked again by utf8.decode at roughly ten times the per-byte cost. This is the counterpoint to exp 235's abandon-on-first-miss lesson — there the fast path was abandoned for the whole remainder; here the 'miss' path is a separate, more expensive decoder that re-reads the value regardless.

This does not reopen exp 258's columnar rewrite or exp 251's decode-bottleneck premise. Both closed on the grounds that a storage-shape change moves work between isolates rather than removing it; this removes work outright and is orthogonal to where the result is stored.
nextSignals: The general shape worth reapplying: any per-cell question the Dart decoder asks while the native step loop already holds the inputs one frame earlier. The decode loop's remaining Dart-side per-cell work is the ExternalTypedData view and the String copy itself; both are VM-owned, so further gains here need a Dart runtime change (a native UTF-8 String entry point, or a non-allocating Pointer view), not another resqlite-side move.

benchmark/experiments/select_rows_text_decode.dart is the durable gate for any future change to the rows-path TEXT decode arm. Keep its int8 control lane (byte-identical code in both arms, so it reads the per-binary offset directly) and its two non-ASCII guards — text8-cjk (ordinary multibyte text) and text4-long-early-nonascii (the worst case for accumulate-then-test: a long value whose only high byte is at offset 0). Run it before touching fastDecodeText, the cell type codes, or resqlite_step_row's TEXT arm.

resqlite_test_text_is_ascii is the classifier's byte-level gate, in the resqlite_test_i64_to_str class: a wrong answer is silent mojibake, not a crash, so any change to the SWAR scan must keep the differential test green.
Cell type codes 1-5 are SQLite's; 6 is now RESQLITE_TEXT_ASCII. A future native-side classification wanting its own code should take 7 and keep the decoder's switch dense.

claims.text: Classifying a TEXT cell as pure ASCII in resqlite_step_row (branch-free SWAR, memcpy-based unaligned loads) instead of in fastDecodeText removes one ExternalTypedData allocation and one bounds-checked Dart scan per cell, worth a reproduced -12.3% / -10.4% on 10k x 8 short-ASCII select(), -14.3% / -10.7% at 40 B, -22.2% / -19.4% at 400 B, and -24.4% / -19.2% on the repo's canonical 6-column mixed row (id INTEGER + 4 TEXT + REAL, from benchmark/shared/seeder.dart). The mixed lane's p50 is its signal; its p90 is noisy across passes and is not a tail regression.
claims.conditions: M1 Pro · AOT CLI bundle · cross-worktree A/B · two order-flipped passes · 31 samples/lane · 2026-08

claims.text: The isolated per-cell mechanism is 6-15 ns, or 12-49% of fastDecodeText's wall depending on payload width (6-14 B: -12% / -34%; 20-40 B: -36% / -39%; 200 B: -49% / -48%). At 80k TEXT cells per lane that is 0.5-1.2 ms, matching the end-to-end deltas in order of magnitude.
claims.conditions: M1 Pro · AOT microbenchmark over malloc'd 8-aligned ASCII payloads · 2026-08

claims.text: An accumulate-then-test SWAR scan that always walks the whole value is not a regression for non-ASCII TEXT. Ordinary CJK text measured -2.4% / -1.7%, and the shape built to expose the trade — a 400 B value with its one multibyte character at byte 0, so the native scan walks the whole payload to learn what the old Dart scan settled in its first word — measured +1.1% / -1.0%. That lane runs ~4.9 ms against ~0.7 ms for the same payload in ASCII: utf8.decode over the value dwarfs a SWAR pass over it, so the 'wasted' scan is an order of magnitude cheaper than the decode it precedes.
claims.conditions: M1 Pro · AOT · 10k x 8 CJK TEXT (~36 B/cell) and 2k x 4 400 B early-nonascii · two order-flipped passes · 2026-08

claims.text: A cross-worktree focused A/B carrying a lane whose code is byte-identical in both arms reads the per-binary layout offset directly. Exp 259's INTEGER-only control moved +0.2% / -2.9% — opposite signs, inside the 3% effect floor — which is what licenses trusting the text lanes without falling back to exp 254's single-binary runtime toggle.
